baseline.authority: docs/design/UI2_0_C3_IDENTITY_SESSIONS_RBAC_CONTRACT.md (FROZEN, PRODUCT OWNER APPROVED, 2026-09-09), section 3.3 row 6: role:security_admin ends another session, ACTIVE -> REVOKED(revoked_by_admin). SessionAdminController implements exactly that action and is already gated to role:security_admin in SecurityWebMvcConfig. Ui2Application.java documents, in its own class-level comment above @ComponentScan, that this controller was deliberately excluded from bean registration pending its collaborators becoming real beans: 'SessionAdminController stays excluded: its own collaborator (a session-admin service) is untouched by this movement and remains out of scope. It is excluded, not deleted: a route that 404s because its controller was never registered is honest, while one that 500s on every call is not.' That stated blocker no longer holds (see engineering).
baseline.engineering: The exclusion comment's own stated blocker -- 'its own collaborator (a session-admin service) is untouched' -- no longer holds. SessionAdminController's constructor now takes exactly SessionRepository and LocalIdentityResolver, and both are already real, wired Spring beans: SessionRepository backs GateChain everywhere, and LocalIdentityResolver has its own @Bean method in LocalAuthenticationConfiguration (localIdentityResolver(LocalCredentialsRepository)). Nothing else in the codebase depends on SessionAdminController being absent from the context; PAN_DISCOVERY_TRUST_PINNED_FINGERPRINT_SHA256 and SecurityWebMvcConfig's ACTION_ID_BY_ROUTE entries for GET /sessions and POST /sessions/revoke are already correct and only need the controller bean to exist to take effect.
baseline.observed: Measured directly against the live deployment after NXS-LOCAL-0362 shipped a Sessions admin screen calling GET /sessions and wiring the existing POST /sessions/revoke: both routes return 404 even from inside the pod with no authentication at all, meaning SessionAdminController was never registered as a Spring bean. Ui2Application.java's own @ComponentScan excludeFilters regex names it explicitly. NXS-LOCAL-0362's own test suite passed because SessionAdminControllerTest constructs the controller directly (new SessionAdminController(...)) rather than through a real Spring context, so the exclusion was invisible to it.
